Usage: rhythm-sightread composer [<vendor/pkg>...] [flags]

Reviews the Composer updates of composer.lock under --path: by default the
newest version each composer.json constraint allows. Names limit it to those
packages; --transitive adds packages you don't require directly. It never runs
the code or any Composer script.

Versions:
  --to <version>                 the candidate version: latest (plugins,
                                 themes), wanted (composer, npm), installed
                                 (against an older --from), x.y.z, an npm
                                 dist-tag, or list to print the published
                                 versions
  --from <version>               the installed version (default: read from
                                 --path, --wp, --from-tuner or the lockfile)
  --to-file <path>               the candidate from a local zip, tgz or folder
                                 at this path (premium plugins, vendor
                                 downloads); marked unverified
  --from-file <path>             the installed version from a local zip, tgz or
                                 folder at this path
  --path <folder>                the site or project folder: a WordPress root or
                                 a folder with lockfiles (default .)
  --wp <command>                 read installed WordPress versions with this
                                 WP-CLI command, e.g. "ssh deploy@host -- wp
                                 --path=/srv/www"
  --from-tuner <report>          read installed plugin and theme versions from a
                                 rhythm-tuner JSON report
  --allow-downgrade              review a --to older than the installed version
  --pre                          let latest and wanted pick pre-releases
  --transitive                   composer and npm: review transitive
                                 dependencies too
  --only <packages>              only these packages: ecosystem IDs or
                                 <eco>:<name> globs, e.g.
                                 wp-plugin:*,npm:@acme/*
  --skip <packages>              leave these packages out (same form as --only)

Sources and integrity:
  --offline                      use cached archives only (RHYTHM_OFFLINE=1 does
                                 the same)
  --allow-unverified             review packages whose integrity couldn't be
                                 checked and let --fail-on pass them
  --allow-partial                let --fail-on pass a run with packages not
                                 checked, fetch failures or timeouts
  --svn-check                    verify themes file by file against
                                 themes.svn.wordpress.org
  --no-osv                       don't ask api.osv.dev for known malicious and
                                 vulnerable versions
  --check-confusion              ask the public registry about private names
                                 (this sends them there)
  --max-size <size>              largest archive to download, a size in KB, MB
                                 or GB (KiB, MiB, GiB); unpacked it may be 4
                                 times that, at most 1GiB (default 256MB)
  --timeout <duration>           how long one request may take (a duration such
                                 as <dur>) (default <dur>)
  --deadline <duration>          how long the whole run may take (a duration
                                 such as <dur>) (default <dur>)
  --retries <n>                  n retries after network errors, 429 and 503
                                 (default 2)
  --jobs <n>                     n packages reviewed in parallel (at most 4
                                 requests per host) (default 4)
  --proxy <url>                  HTTP proxy url (default HTTPS_PROXY)
  -A, --user-agent <header>      the User-Agent header (default
                                 rhythm-sightread/<version>
                                 (+https://github.com/RhythmShahriar/sightread))

Signals:
  --signals <folder>             load extra signal YAML from this folder
                                 (repeatable)
  --no-signal-updates            use the built-in signals and names, not a newer
                                 downloaded pack
  --id <ids>                     show only findings with these signal ids
                                 (globs); the others still count for the verdict
                                 and --fail-on
  --exclude-id <ids>             hide findings with these signal ids (globs),
                                 never integrity or allow signals; they still
                                 count for the verdict and --fail-on
  --severity <level>             hide findings below this level: info, low,
                                 medium, high or critical; they still count for
                                 the verdict and --fail-on (default info)
  --min-confidence <confidence>
                                 confidence a finding needs to count: confirmed
                                 or likely (config min_confidence) (default
                                 likely)
  --min-age <duration>           fresh-release fires for a candidate younger
                                 than this duration (config min_age) (default
                                 72h)

Gate:
  --fail-on <level>              exit 1 on a finding at or above this level:
                                 none, info, low, medium, high or critical
                                 (config fail_on; default none)
  --baseline <report>            hide findings already in this saved JSON report
  --no-allow                     ignore .sightread/allowed.yaml for this run
  --config <file>                config file (default: the nearest
                                 .sightread/config.yaml here or above)
  --no-config                    read no config, for folders you don't trust

Output:
  --json                         print the rhythm-sightread/v1 JSON report
  --jsonl                        print one JSON line per update as it finishes,
                                 then the summary
  --md                           print Markdown for pull requests and job
                                 summaries
  --html                         print a standalone HTML report with the full
                                 diff
  --sarif                        print SARIF 2.1.0 for GitHub code scanning
  -o, --output <file>            also write the report to this file, format from
                                 .json .jsonl .md .html or .sarif (repeatable;
                                 written once complete)
  --open                         open the HTML report when done
  --diff                         print every changed hunk, not just the ones
                                 findings point at
  --max-findings <n>             n findings shown per update on the terminal
                                 (default 10)
  --sign                         sign the JSON report (<file>.json.sig, Ed25519)
  --redact-paths                 write paths relative to the target or ~
                                 (default on when CI is set)
  -q, --quiet                    verdicts and findings only
  --plain                        no color, boxes or glyphs (also when stdout is
                                 not a terminal)
  --no-color                     no color (NO_COLOR does the same)
  -v, --verbose                  every request, hash and program started to
                                 stderr, header values masked

Soundcheck:
  --soundcheck <url>             install the update on this staging url and
                                 compare it before and after with
                                 rhythm-soundcheck
  --apply <command>              composer and npm, or a remote --wp: the command
                                 that installs the update on staging
  --rollback                     reinstall the reviewed old version when
                                 Soundcheck finds changes at
                                 --soundcheck-fail-on
  --soundcheck-fail-on <class>   Soundcheck change class that fails: broke, new
                                 or changed (default broke)
  --soundcheck-anyway            install on staging even when the update is on
                                 HOLD
  --skip-roadie-verify           don't check the staging copy with rhythm-roadie
                                 verify (the report says so)

Examples:
  rhythm-sightread composer --path api
  rhythm-sightread composer monolog/monolog --to 3.12.1
  rhythm-sightread composer --transitive --md -o composer.md

Arguments after -- go to rhythm-soundcheck snapshot.
